Functions and formulas

Add formulas & functions

Want advanced Google Workspace features for your business?

Try Google Workspace today!

You can use functions and formulas to automate calculations in Google Sheets.

Tip: If you’re already familiar with functions and formulas and just need to know which ones are available, go to Google Sheets function reference.

Add formulas and functions to a spreadsheet

To get an example spreadsheet and follow along with the video, click “Make a Copy” below.

Make a copy

Use a formula
  • Open a spreadsheet.
  • Type an equal sign (=) in a cell and type in the function you want to use. Note: You may see suggested formulas and ranges based on your data.

A function help box will be visible throughout the editing process to provide you with a definition of the function and its syntax, as well as an example for reference. If you need more information, click the “Learn more” link at the bottom of the help box to open a full article.

Tip: You might get suggestions to help you complete formulas with the relevant functions. You can accept or reject these suggestions.

To turn formula suggestions on or off, at the top, click Tools Suggestion controls Enable formula suggestions.

You might find correction suggestions in previously compiled data and analyses, to improve confidence in insights. You can accept or reject these suggestions.

To turn formula corrections on or off, at the top, click Tools Suggestion controls Enable formula corrections.

Additional features for creating formulas

Simple ways to select and edit ranges

Range-selection mode
  • When editing a formula, the range-selection signal (a grey bracket) will appear next to your cursor where you’re likely to need a range in the formula. When you see the signal, you can move the keyboard arrows around your sheet to select a range.
  • Toggle this mode on and off using the keyboard shortcuts F2 or Ctrl + e. If range-selection mode is turned off, use the arrow keys to move your cursor inside the input box instead of selecting a range.
  • You can also click within the sheet to select a range when editing a formula.
Range replacement
  • When you have the text of a range highlighted in your formula, use F2 or Ctrl + e to enter range-selection mode and easily make adjustments to the range.
  • If you press Shift + F2 or Shift + Ctrl + e while editing the text of a range, you can easily make adjustments to all occurrences of that range in the formula. Tip: You can also select ranges for your formula that are non-adjacent. To select multiple cells, click and hold Ctrl on your keyboard (Cmd on a Mac) as you select the cells you want to include in the formula.
Formula corrections

If there are errors after you apply a formula to a range, a “Formula correction” box may appear with a suggested fix.

To accept or reject suggestions, you can

  • Click Accept or Dismiss .

  • Press Crtl + Enter or Cmd + Return (on a Mac). To turn Formula correction on or off:

  • At the top left, click Tools Autocomplete.

  • Click Enable formula corrections. Nested functions

A function used in the same cell with another function is called a nested function. When functions are combined, Google Sheets will calculate the innermost function first. The nested function is contained in parentheses and is used as one of the components of the surrounding function.

For example, let’s say you want to calculate the absolute value of a sum of several numbers in the cell range A1:A7. To calculate the sum of these numbers, you would enter ‘=SUM(A1:A7)’ into a cell.

To calculate the absolute value of this sum, you need to nest the sum formula within absolute value formula. To calculate both formulas in a single cell, enter ‘=ABS(SUM(A1:A7))’ into the cell. Note that the =SUM() function is performed first and is used as a component in the =ABS() function.

Formula highlighting

When you reference other cells in a formula, those cells will be highlighted in contrasting colors to help you more easily build a formula. When you click on a cell that contains a completed formula, you’ll also see these cells highlighted.

Change the formula bar size

To make the formula bar bigger or smaller, click the bottom of it, then drag it up or down.

Note: You can also use keyboard shortcuts to change the size. Click the formula bar, then click:

  • PC: Ctrl + Up and Ctrl + Down
  • Mac: Ctrl + Option + Up and Ctrl + Option + Down Functions that don’t work

Some functions from other spreadsheet programs don’t work in Sheets.

Type

Description

CALL

Calls a dynamic link library or code resource. Since this resource might not be available on all devices, Sheets doesn’t use this function.

Tip: You can use macros or Apps Script instead.

CUBE functions (CUBEKPIMEMBER, CUBEMEMBER, CUBEMEMBERPROPERTY)

Lets you use Excel’s CUBE data model.

Tip: If you want to use similar CUBEs, you can use the Data Connectors feature.

INFO

Returns information about the Sheets document file, such as its filepath.

Note: Because Sheets emphasizes online collaboration, much of the information from this method may not be available or the most transparent to all users.

REGISTER.ID

Gets the registry ID from Windows.

Note: Since Sheets isn’t linked to any one operating system, this function isn’t supported.

RTD

Gets data from a Component Object Model (COM) Automation server.

Tip: Since everyone can’t get to the COM server, you can use macros or Apps Script.

WEBSERVICE

Relies on Windows to work fully.

Note: Since Sheets isn’t linked to any one operating system, this function isn’t supported.

Reference data from other sheets

Want advanced Google Workspace features for your business?

Try Google Workspace today!

Within a single spreadsheet, you can replicate data and copy it from one sheet to another.

Get data from other sheets in your spreadsheet
  • On your computer, go to docs.google.com/spreadsheets/.
  • Open or create a sheet.
  • Select a cell.
  • Type= followed by the sheet name, an exclamation point, and the cell being copied. For example, =Sheet1!A1 or ='Sheet number two'!B4. Note: If a sheet name contains spaces or other non-alphanumeric symbols, include single quotes around it (as in the second example).
Get data from other spreadsheets

Important: To reference a cell or range of cells in another spreadsheet, you must use the IMPORTRANGE function.

To pull data from other spreadsheets, use the IMPORTRANGE function.

Get data from other spreadsheets

Important: To reference a cell or range of cells in another spreadsheet, you must use the IMPORTRANGE function.

To pull data from other spreadsheets, use the IMPORTRANGE function.

Reference data from other sheets (iPhone and iPad)

Want advanced Google Workspace features for your business?

Within a single spreadsheet, you can replicate data and copy it from one sheet to another.

Get data from other sheets in your spreadsheet
  • On your iPhone or iPad, open the Google Sheets app .
  • Open or create a sheet.
  • Select a cell.
  • Type = followed by the sheet name, an exclamation point, and the cell being copied. For example, =Sheet1!A1 or ='Sheet number two'!B4. Note: If a sheet name contains spaces or other non-alphanumeric symbols, include single quotes around it (as in the second example).
Get data from other worksheets

Important: To reference a cell or range of cells in another spreadsheet, you must use the IMPORTRANGE function.

To pull data from other spreadsheets, open docs.google.com on your computer and use the IMPORTRANGE function.

Gemini in Docs Editors

Collaborate with Gemini in Google Sheets (Computer)

With Gemini in Google Sheets, you can:

  • Create tables.
  • Create formulas.
  • Generate data analysis and insights.
  • Build charts and graphs.
  • Summarize your emails and files from Drive and Gmail.
  • Chat about and analyze large datasets in BigQuery.
  • Perform actions like:
    • Apply conditional formatting.
    • Create a pivot table.
    • Add a dropdown or checkbox.
    • Sort, apply, or clear a filter.
    • Find and replace text.
    • Set a number format.
    • Insert, delete, or freeze rows and columns.
    • Fill a range.
    • Format a table.
    • Solve optimization tasks. Feature availability:
  • This feature requires an eligible Google Workspace or Google AI plan. Learn how to get started with Google Workspace with Gemini.
  • This feature is also available through our trusted tester program, Google Workspace Experiments.
  • Learn about supported languages for Google Workspace with Gemini.
Get started with Gemini in Sheets

Important: This feature works best with native Google Sheets files. To use Gemini features in an Excel file (.xlsx), select File Save as Google Sheets.

  • On your computer, open a spreadsheet from Google Sheets.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • In the side panel, select a suggested prompt or write your own prompt. Select a suggestion
    • Select from the list of suggestions.
      • To get more options, select More suggestions.
    • At the bottom, in the prompt box, replace the example text with the information you want.
    • Press Enter.
  • Enter a prompt in Gemini
    • At the bottom, in the prompt box, enter a prompt.
    • Press Enter.
  • Optional:
    • To reverse an action, click Undo .
    • To remove your history, click More options Clear history.
  • Optional: You can use multiple tabs in a single prompt. To focus Gemini’s attention on a specific tab:
    • In the side panel, check the dropdown menu in the prompt box.
    • From the dropdown menu, make sure only the tabs you want to use are selected.
      • To use all available sources again, click Reset to all sources . This applies after you deselect sources.
    • Enter your prompt. Tips:
  • To avoid losing your history, insert generated output in the spreadsheet. You lose your conversation history when:
    • You reload your browser.
    • You close and reopen the spreadsheet.
    • Your computer goes offline.
  • For a more comprehensive analysis, you can choose to focus Gemini’s attention on specific tables when there are multiple tables in Sheets.

Things to ask Gemini in Sheets

Summarize spreadsheet with Gemini

When you open a spreadsheet that has data, in the side panel, you’ll find a summary of your spreadsheet.

You can:

  • To show the whole summary of the suggested content, click View more.

  • To send feedback about the suggested text, click Good suggestion or Bad suggestion . You can also ask Gemini to:

  • Understand your spreadsheet better. Examples of prompt:

    • “Summarize this spreadsheet.”
    • “Explain this spreadsheet like I’m 5 years old.” To summarize a spreadsheet, you can use these shortcuts:

  • For Mac: Press ⌘ + Ctrl + n

  • For Windows: Press Ctrl + Alt + n Create tables with Gemini

You can use Gemini to create tables in Sheets.

  • On your computer, open a spreadsheet from Google Sheets.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • In the side panel, select a prompt or create your own. Examples of prompt:
    • “Create a table for a full day team event.”
    • “Create a trip plan for a vacation in a national park.”
    • “Create a social media tracker for marketing.”
  • Press Enter.
  • (Optional):
    • To add the table to your spreadsheet, click Insert .
    • To see a different version, click Retry .
    • To refine before inserting a table, you can add follow-up prompts. Examples of prompt:
      • “Add another 5 rows of different activities.”
      • “Add details on cost.”
    • To send feedback about the suggested table, click Good suggestion or Bad suggestion . Create formulas with Gemini

You can use Gemini to generate formulas in Sheets.

  • On your computer, open a spreadsheet from Google Sheets.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
    • You can also start from any cell and enter =.
    • Then use a shortcut:
      • For Windows and Chrome OS: Ctrl + Alt + g
      • For Mac OS: ⌘ + Ctrl + g
  • In the side panel, create your own prompt using references from your sheet, or generic cell names. Examples of prompts:
    • “Create a formula that divides goals by games.”
    • “Create a formula to find cell C1 in range D:G and output value in column G.”
  • (Optional):
    • To add the formula to your spreadsheet, click the cell you’d like to insert this formula, click Insert .
    • To see a different version, click Retry .
    • To send feedback about the suggested table, click Good suggestion or Bad suggestion .
Fix formula errors with Gemini

When you create a formula and a cell shows an error message:

  • Hover over the cell.
  • Click Fix.
  • Gemini reviews the formula and analyzes the issue.
    • To cancel the operation, in the side panel, click Stop . Create images with Gemini

You can ask Gemini to generate images in Sheets.

  • On your computer, open a spreadsheet from Google Sheets.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • On the side panel, create your own prompt.
    • Example: “Create an image of a dog with glasses.”
  • On the image that you like, you can hover over to:
    • Insert an image: Click Insert .
    • Find similar images: Click Generate more .
  • You can also:
    • Find more images: At the bottom, click Generate more .
    • Change your prompt: Click Edit prompt .
    • Send feedback about the generated images: At the bottom, click Good suggestion or Bad suggestion . Generate data analysis & insights with Gemini

You can use Gemini to answer questions about the data in your sheet.

  • On your computer, open a spreadsheet from Google Sheets.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • In the side panel, create your own prompt with references from your sheet or generic cell names. Examples of prompts:
    • “Identify trends in this table.”
    • “How can I show regression and prediction of this data?”
    • “What analysis can you help me perform with this sheet?”
    • “Help me understand month-to-month food prices.”
  • Optional:
    • To check the analysis steps: Click Analysis steps .
    • To export to a new Google docs: Click Export to Docs . Generate charts & graphs with Gemini

You can use Gemini to generate charts and graphs.

  • On your computer, open a spreadsheet from Google Sheets.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • In the side panel, create your own prompt with references from your sheet or generic cell names. Examples of prompts:
    • “Create a chart with date on the x-axis and total on the y-axis.”
    • “Make a line chart.”
    • “Create a graph that shows the percentage of expenses on the total stipend after tax.”
    • “Make a chart analyzing my expenses for the month.”
  • Optional:
    • To preview the chart: Click Preview .
    • To copy the chart: Click More options Copy chart .
    • To check the analysis steps: Click Analysis steps .
    • To export to a new Google docs: Click Export to Docs .
  • To insert the chart into the sheet, click Insert .
    • When you insert a chart, it’s added to a new tab along with its underlying data.
    • At the bottom left, a message displays to confirm the insertion of a new tab. It also gives you an option to delete the newly inserted tab.
    • The chart is linked to the new tab’s data and is fully editable. Tip: The generated chart doesn’t link or respond to changes in the original data set that was used to generate it. If you create a chart from a BigQuery Connected Sheet, the chart stays connected and automatically updates with the latest data when you refresh it.

Discover and connect your external data sources

You can use Gemini in Google Sheets to query available data sources and import external data directly into your spreadsheets via third-party connectors.

Important: Your Google Workspace administrator has controls to enable or disable connectors for your organization. To access third-party connectors in Sheets, you must have enabled and logged into the connectors in Google Workspace Marketplace. Learn more about using connectors with Gemini in Workspace.

  • On your computer, open a spreadsheet in Google Sheets.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • In the side panel, enter a prompt to explore data connector options or import data. For example:
    • “@[source name] what type of data can I import?”
    • “Import [data] from @[source name].” Data will then be imported as a table to your spreadsheet.

Analyze and import data from connected sources

You can use Gemini in Google Sheets to analyze large datasets connected through BigQuery or import data from third-party apps.

Analyze BigQuery data in Connected Sheets

You can use Gemini in Sheets to ask questions, analyze and explore data trends, and build live, connected charts, pivot tables, formulas and more across your full BigQuery dataset. Learn more about analyzing BigQuery data in Connected Sheets.

Important:

  • To query BigQuery data with Gemini, you need access to BigQuery and a Google Cloud billing project. Learn more about using BigQuery with Google Sheets.

  • Collaborators who have view access to the spreadsheet without BigQuery permissions can still view saved results, charts, and dashboards in the sheet. Running new queries or refreshes requires BigQuery access. Learn more about BigQuery permissions.

  • Gemini runs read-only queries on your connected BigQuery data source and doesn’t modify or delete data in BigQuery. Get started with Gemini on BigQuery data

  • Open Google Sheets.

  • Open a spreadsheet connected to BigQuery data.

    • Learn how to open a BigQuery project in Google Sheets.

  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .

  • In the side panel, select a prompt or create your own. Examples of prompts:

    • “Compare our top 5 marketing campaigns month over month.”
    • “Make a bar chart of clicks by campaign.”
    • “Build an executive dashboard tab with revenue by region, a monthly trend chart, and an extract of urgent tickets.”
    • “Check current stock levels in BigQuery for the Product IDs listed in Column A.”

  • Press Enter.

    • Note: If you’re using this feature for the first time, you may need to follow steps in the side panel to authenticate your account.

  • Optional: You can ask follow-up questions to explore further, or ask Gemini to create or update items in your spreadsheet.

  • When you’re done prompting, review the plan card in the side panel and click Apply. Tips: Charts, pivot tables, formulas, and extracts created by Gemini stay connected to BigQuery. You can update them anytime manually or with a scheduled refresh. Learn more about refreshing your BigQuery data.

Perform actions in Google Sheets with Gemini

  • On your computer, open a spreadsheet from Google Sheets.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • To edit your spreadsheet through prompts, in the side panel, enter a prompt that describes the action you want to perform. Example of a prompt:
    • “Highlight values below 100”
  • Gemini generates an “Action preview card” with details of the proposed action. On the “Action preview card,” click Apply.
    • The preview card changes to a “Working on it…” dialog box.
  • Once the action is complete, the Settings and Undo buttons show.
    • Settings: If available, you can configure actions, like adjust pivot table parameters or conditional formatting rules, when you click Settings .
      • This is only available for actions with configurable settings.
    • Undo: If the action doesn’t give the result you want, click Undo .
      • This is available until you make further changes.
Ask Gemini to perform the following actions:

Apply conditional formatting

You can highlight cells based on specific criteria, like values below a certain number or duplicate entries.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Examples of prompts:

  • “Highlight rows where sales are greater than 500”
  • “Add conditional formatting to highlight dates in the past” Create new dropdowns

You can create dropdown lists in specified ranges or convert existing data to dropdown lists.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Examples of prompts:

  • “Create a dropdown in column A with options ‘High,’ ‘Medium,’ ‘Low’”
  • “Convert column B to a dropdown with values from column C” Tip: When the location of the new dropdown list isn’t specified, the new dropdown list created will be added to the rightmost empty column.

Create a new pivot table

You can create a pivot table to summarize data in a new sheet or the specified range.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Create a pivot table that shows the sum of sales by region”
  • “Create a pivot with Status in column A, value as task counts, and columns for Priority” Apply filters

You can apply filters to the active table context.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Filter for sales greater than $1,000” Sort your spreadsheet

You can sort the active table context.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Sort by date in descending order” Add checkbox

You can insert a checkbox into a specific cell or range of cells to track tasks with two-options states like “yes/no.”

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Add a checkbox at the beginning of the table and name it ‘WATCHED’.”
  • “Insert a checkbox in cell B5 and make sure it’s unchecked by default.” Find and replace

You can automate the process of searching for a specific text or value within a dataset and replacing it with a new one.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Find all instances of ‘Grass’ in the ‘Data converted into Sheet Format’ sheet and replace them with ‘Grass court’.”
  • “In column I, find every occurrence of the word ‘Clay’ and replace it with ‘Clay court’.” Delete dimension

You can remove a column or a row from a dataset.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Delete the ‘TOURNAMENT_SURFACE’ column from the ‘Data converted into Sheet Format’ sheet.”
  • “Remove the row with the year ‘2021’.” Fill range

You can fill a specified range of cells with a single value or a repeating pattern.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Fill the cells in the ‘YEAR’ column from A2 to A22 with the value ‘1’.”
  • “Copy the value from cell H17 and apply it to the entire range from H18 to H22.” Insert dimension

You can create a new empty column or row at a specified location.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Insert a new column named ‘ATP_RANKING_DIFF’ between the ‘RUNNER-UP_ATP_RANKING’ and ‘WINNER_LEFT_OR_RIGHT_HANDED’ columns.”
  • “Add a new row at the bottom of the table.” Clear filter

You can remove any filters currently applied to a dataset to view all data entries.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Remove all filters from the ‘TOURNAMENT_SURFACE’ to view the complete data set.”
  • “Clear the filter that’s currently applied to the ‘NATIONALITY’ column.” Format as table

You can apply a table style to a selected range of data.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Format the data range from J2 to J22 with comma and dollar sign.”
  • “Apply a table style to the selected data to make it easier to read.” Set number format

You can display numerical values in a cell or range of cells.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Change the number format for the ‘WINNER_PRIZE’ column to display currency with two decimal places.” Freeze dimension

You can lock a specific row or column in place to make it visible on the screen even when you scroll through the rest of the spreadsheet.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Freeze the top row of the ‘Data converted into Sheet Format’ sheet to make the headers visible.”
  • “Lock the first two columns of the ‘Data converted into Sheet Format’ to keep the ‘YEAR,’ ‘TOURNAMENT,’ and ‘WINNER’ visible while scrolling to the right.” Perform multi-step tasks

To handle complex requests and complete multiple tasks at the same time, combine several actions in a single prompt.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Examples of prompts:

  • “Clean up this tracker: make the status and priority columns into dropdowns. Add new columns at the end of the table: a new formula column for”Days until due date” (formatted as a number) and a checkbox column for Completed. Finally, highlight due dates in the next two weeks!”
  • “Delete rows where the notes show the seller moved to a new team, highlight in light green sellers achieving more than 120% of quota, then add a new”Notes” column.”
  • “Delete rows where status is archived. Add a new”Team” column between task name and assignee and populate it with a dropdown of Animal themed team names.” Summarize your Drive files with Gemini

You can use Gemini to reference files from your Drive to generate responses in Sheets.

  • On your computer, open a spreadsheet from Google Sheets.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • In the side panel, ask Gemini to use your Drive files to generate text.
    • Example: “What are the main points of: Meeting Notes: Core Team sync.”
  • To check which files were used, below the response, click Expand Sources.
  • (Optional):
    • To add the text to your spreadsheet, click Insert .
    • To view an another version, click Retry .
    • To send feedback about the suggested text, click Good suggestion or Bad suggestion . Summarize your Gmail emails with Gemini

You can use Gemini to reference emails you sent to generate responses.

  • On your computer, open a spreadsheet from Google Sheets.
  • At the top right, click Gemini in Sheets side panel .
  • In the side panel, provide your prompt asking Gemini to reference Gmail email(s).
    • Example: “Catch me up on the latest Monthly Review emails.”
  • To check which files were used, below the response, click Expand Sources.
  • (Optional):
    • To add the text to your spreadsheet, click Insert .
    • To generate a new suggestion, click Retry .
    • To send feedback about the suggested text, click Good suggestion or Bad suggestion . Get help with Google Sheets
  • “Teach me how to use conditional formatting with a color scale.”
  • “How can I remove duplicates?” Get answers from the web

Important: To get answers from the web, make sure to include phrases like “Use Google Search” or “Using web search” in your prompt.

  • “Write a paragraph describing the weather today in Mountain View, California using web search.”
  • “Help me write a paragraph explaining if lightning can strike the same place twice using only information from the web.” Use a Gem

Important: Not all languages support Gems. Learn more about supported languages for Google Workspace with Gemini.

  • On your computer, at the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • On the right, in the side panel, click Gems.
  • Click the Gem you want to use.
  • Select a custom or premade Gem.
    • To start a conversation with the Gem, type a question or prompt at the bottom. Tip: To create a Gem, go to gemini.google.com. You can then use your Gem in the Gemini app and Gemini side panel. Learn how to use Gems in Gemini Apps.

Use Optimization problem solver

You can use the Optimization problem solver to solve operations and logistics tasks, such as allocating budgets, scheduling staff, or optimizing supply chains.

  • On your computer, open a spreadsheet in Google Sheets.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • In the side panel, describe your optimization problem. Example prompts:
    • “I want you to solve a capital budgeting problem. Your main goal is to select the best portfolio of projects to maximize the total Net Present Value.”
    • “I need to minimize total supplier spend. Adjust the order quantities for each supplier to meet my total demand of 1,000 units. Make sure no single supplier provides more than 40% of the total volume.”
    • “I need help with a staffing problem. Determine the minimum number of employees to hire for each of my 7 shift patterns to minimize my total weekly payroll. I must meet my daily staffing requirements, and each employee costs $1,200 per week.”
  • Press Enter.
Give feedback on generated output

Google Workspace with Gemini is constantly learning and may not be able to support your request.

If you get a suggestion that’s inaccurate or that you feel is unsafe, you can let us know by submitting feedback.

  • To provide feedback on the generated input of this feature, click , and follow the prompts.
  • To provide general feedback on this feature, at the top, go to Help Help Docs improve.
  • To report a legal issue, learn how to report content for legal reasons.
Collaborate with Gemini on shared or external spreadsheets

You might see a message in the side panel that says, “Warning: Content added by Gemini may be visible to users outside your domain. Use caution with prompts and before enabling search settings.” This message means one of the following:

  • The file has an out-of-domain user with view or edit permissions.
  • The file was created by an out-of-domain user. The file will remain to be classified as “externally accessible” even if the original author(s) removed themselves from the access list.
Learn about Gemini feature suggestions
  • Gemini feature suggestions don’t represent Google’s views, and should not be attributed to Google.
  • Don’t rely on Gemini features as medical, legal, financial or other professional advice.
  • Gemini features may suggest inaccurate or inappropriate information. Your feedback makes Gemini more helpful and safe.
  • Enterprise end users can submit feedback about their experience using this feature. End users are informed before they submit feedback that the feedback data shouldn’t contain personal, sensitive, or confidential information.
  • Your conversations with Gemini in Sheets are not saved to Gemini Activity. When you delete your Gemini in Sheets conversation history, it doesn’t delete any information that is saved to your Gemini Activity. Learn how to delete your Gemini Activity.

Bad suggestion

Show code

Hide code

Things to ask Gemini in Sheets

Summarize spreadsheet with Gemini

When you open a spreadsheet that has data, in the side panel, you’ll find a summary of your spreadsheet.

You can:

  • To show the whole summary of the suggested content, click View more.

  • To send feedback about the suggested text, click Good suggestion or Bad suggestion . You can also ask Gemini to:

  • Understand your spreadsheet better. Examples of prompt:

    • “Summarize this spreadsheet.”
    • “Explain this spreadsheet like I’m 5 years old.” To summarize a spreadsheet, you can use these shortcuts:

  • For Mac: Press ⌘ + Ctrl + n

  • For Windows: Press Ctrl + Alt + n Create tables with Gemini

You can use Gemini to create tables in Sheets.

  • On your computer, open a spreadsheet from Google Sheets.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • In the side panel, select a prompt or create your own. Examples of prompt:
    • “Create a table for a full day team event.”
    • “Create a trip plan for a vacation in a national park.”
    • “Create a social media tracker for marketing.”
  • Press Enter.
  • (Optional):
    • To add the table to your spreadsheet, click Insert .
    • To see a different version, click Retry .
    • To refine before inserting a table, you can add follow-up prompts. Examples of prompt:
      • “Add another 5 rows of different activities.”
      • “Add details on cost.”
    • To send feedback about the suggested table, click Good suggestion or Bad suggestion . Create formulas with Gemini

You can use Gemini to generate formulas in Sheets.

  • On your computer, open a spreadsheet from Google Sheets.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
    • You can also start from any cell and enter =.
    • Then use a shortcut:
      • For Windows and Chrome OS: Ctrl + Alt + g
      • For Mac OS: ⌘ + Ctrl + g
  • In the side panel, create your own prompt using references from your sheet, or generic cell names. Examples of prompts:
    • “Create a formula that divides goals by games.”
    • “Create a formula to find cell C1 in range D:G and output value in column G.”
  • (Optional):
    • To add the formula to your spreadsheet, click the cell you’d like to insert this formula, click Insert .
    • To see a different version, click Retry .
    • To send feedback about the suggested table, click Good suggestion or Bad suggestion .
Fix formula errors with Gemini

When you create a formula and a cell shows an error message:

  • Hover over the cell.
  • Click Fix.
  • Gemini reviews the formula and analyzes the issue.
    • To cancel the operation, in the side panel, click Stop . Create images with Gemini

You can ask Gemini to generate images in Sheets.

  • On your computer, open a spreadsheet from Google Sheets.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • On the side panel, create your own prompt.
    • Example: “Create an image of a dog with glasses.”
  • On the image that you like, you can hover over to:
    • Insert an image: Click Insert .
    • Find similar images: Click Generate more .
  • You can also:
    • Find more images: At the bottom, click Generate more .
    • Change your prompt: Click Edit prompt .
    • Send feedback about the generated images: At the bottom, click Good suggestion or Bad suggestion . Generate data analysis & insights with Gemini

You can use Gemini to answer questions about the data in your sheet.

  • On your computer, open a spreadsheet from Google Sheets.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • In the side panel, create your own prompt with references from your sheet or generic cell names. Examples of prompts:
    • “Identify trends in this table.”
    • “How can I show regression and prediction of this data?”
    • “What analysis can you help me perform with this sheet?”
    • “Help me understand month-to-month food prices.”
  • Optional:
    • To check the analysis steps: Click Analysis steps .
    • To export to a new Google docs: Click Export to Docs . Generate charts & graphs with Gemini

You can use Gemini to generate charts and graphs.

  • On your computer, open a spreadsheet from Google Sheets.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • In the side panel, create your own prompt with references from your sheet or generic cell names. Examples of prompts:
    • “Create a chart with date on the x-axis and total on the y-axis.”
    • “Make a line chart.”
    • “Create a graph that shows the percentage of expenses on the total stipend after tax.”
    • “Make a chart analyzing my expenses for the month.”
  • Optional:
    • To preview the chart: Click Preview .
    • To copy the chart: Click More options Copy chart .
    • To check the analysis steps: Click Analysis steps .
    • To export to a new Google docs: Click Export to Docs .
  • To insert the chart into the sheet, click Insert .
    • When you insert a chart, it’s added to a new tab along with its underlying data.
    • At the bottom left, a message displays to confirm the insertion of a new tab. It also gives you an option to delete the newly inserted tab.
    • The chart is linked to the new tab’s data and is fully editable. Tip: The generated chart doesn’t link or respond to changes in the original data set that was used to generate it. If you create a chart from a BigQuery Connected Sheet, the chart stays connected and automatically updates with the latest data when you refresh it.

Discover and connect your external data sources

You can use Gemini in Google Sheets to query available data sources and import external data directly into your spreadsheets via third-party connectors.

Important: Your Google Workspace administrator has controls to enable or disable connectors for your organization. To access third-party connectors in Sheets, you must have enabled and logged into the connectors in Google Workspace Marketplace. Learn more about using connectors with Gemini in Workspace.

  • On your computer, open a spreadsheet in Google Sheets.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • In the side panel, enter a prompt to explore data connector options or import data. For example:
    • “@[source name] what type of data can I import?”
    • “Import [data] from @[source name].” Data will then be imported as a table to your spreadsheet.

Analyze and import data from connected sources

You can use Gemini in Google Sheets to analyze large datasets connected through BigQuery or import data from third-party apps.

Analyze BigQuery data in Connected Sheets

You can use Gemini in Sheets to ask questions, analyze and explore data trends, and build live, connected charts, pivot tables, formulas and more across your full BigQuery dataset. Learn more about analyzing BigQuery data in Connected Sheets.

Important:

  • To query BigQuery data with Gemini, you need access to BigQuery and a Google Cloud billing project. Learn more about using BigQuery with Google Sheets.

  • Collaborators who have view access to the spreadsheet without BigQuery permissions can still view saved results, charts, and dashboards in the sheet. Running new queries or refreshes requires BigQuery access. Learn more about BigQuery permissions.

  • Gemini runs read-only queries on your connected BigQuery data source and doesn’t modify or delete data in BigQuery. Get started with Gemini on BigQuery data

  • Open Google Sheets.

  • Open a spreadsheet connected to BigQuery data.

    • Learn how to open a BigQuery project in Google Sheets.

  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .

  • In the side panel, select a prompt or create your own. Examples of prompts:

    • “Compare our top 5 marketing campaigns month over month.”
    • “Make a bar chart of clicks by campaign.”
    • “Build an executive dashboard tab with revenue by region, a monthly trend chart, and an extract of urgent tickets.”
    • “Check current stock levels in BigQuery for the Product IDs listed in Column A.”

  • Press Enter.

    • Note: If you’re using this feature for the first time, you may need to follow steps in the side panel to authenticate your account.

  • Optional: You can ask follow-up questions to explore further, or ask Gemini to create or update items in your spreadsheet.

  • When you’re done prompting, review the plan card in the side panel and click Apply. Tips: Charts, pivot tables, formulas, and extracts created by Gemini stay connected to BigQuery. You can update them anytime manually or with a scheduled refresh. Learn more about refreshing your BigQuery data.

Perform actions in Google Sheets with Gemini

  • On your computer, open a spreadsheet from Google Sheets.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • To edit your spreadsheet through prompts, in the side panel, enter a prompt that describes the action you want to perform. Example of a prompt:
    • “Highlight values below 100”
  • Gemini generates an “Action preview card” with details of the proposed action. On the “Action preview card,” click Apply.
    • The preview card changes to a “Working on it…” dialog box.
  • Once the action is complete, the Settings and Undo buttons show.
    • Settings: If available, you can configure actions, like adjust pivot table parameters or conditional formatting rules, when you click Settings .
      • This is only available for actions with configurable settings.
    • Undo: If the action doesn’t give the result you want, click Undo .
      • This is available until you make further changes.
Ask Gemini to perform the following actions:

Apply conditional formatting

You can highlight cells based on specific criteria, like values below a certain number or duplicate entries.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Examples of prompts:

  • “Highlight rows where sales are greater than 500”
  • “Add conditional formatting to highlight dates in the past” Create new dropdowns

You can create dropdown lists in specified ranges or convert existing data to dropdown lists.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Examples of prompts:

  • “Create a dropdown in column A with options ‘High,’ ‘Medium,’ ‘Low’”
  • “Convert column B to a dropdown with values from column C” Tip: When the location of the new dropdown list isn’t specified, the new dropdown list created will be added to the rightmost empty column.

Create a new pivot table

You can create a pivot table to summarize data in a new sheet or the specified range.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Create a pivot table that shows the sum of sales by region”
  • “Create a pivot with Status in column A, value as task counts, and columns for Priority” Apply filters

You can apply filters to the active table context.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Filter for sales greater than $1,000” Sort your spreadsheet

You can sort the active table context.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Sort by date in descending order” Add checkbox

You can insert a checkbox into a specific cell or range of cells to track tasks with two-options states like “yes/no.”

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Add a checkbox at the beginning of the table and name it ‘WATCHED’.”
  • “Insert a checkbox in cell B5 and make sure it’s unchecked by default.” Find and replace

You can automate the process of searching for a specific text or value within a dataset and replacing it with a new one.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Find all instances of ‘Grass’ in the ‘Data converted into Sheet Format’ sheet and replace them with ‘Grass court’.”
  • “In column I, find every occurrence of the word ‘Clay’ and replace it with ‘Clay court’.” Delete dimension

You can remove a column or a row from a dataset.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Delete the ‘TOURNAMENT_SURFACE’ column from the ‘Data converted into Sheet Format’ sheet.”
  • “Remove the row with the year ‘2021’.” Fill range

You can fill a specified range of cells with a single value or a repeating pattern.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Fill the cells in the ‘YEAR’ column from A2 to A22 with the value ‘1’.”
  • “Copy the value from cell H17 and apply it to the entire range from H18 to H22.” Insert dimension

You can create a new empty column or row at a specified location.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Insert a new column named ‘ATP_RANKING_DIFF’ between the ‘RUNNER-UP_ATP_RANKING’ and ‘WINNER_LEFT_OR_RIGHT_HANDED’ columns.”
  • “Add a new row at the bottom of the table.” Clear filter

You can remove any filters currently applied to a dataset to view all data entries.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Remove all filters from the ‘TOURNAMENT_SURFACE’ to view the complete data set.”
  • “Clear the filter that’s currently applied to the ‘NATIONALITY’ column.” Format as table

You can apply a table style to a selected range of data.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Format the data range from J2 to J22 with comma and dollar sign.”
  • “Apply a table style to the selected data to make it easier to read.” Set number format

You can display numerical values in a cell or range of cells.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Change the number format for the ‘WINNER_PRIZE’ column to display currency with two decimal places.” Freeze dimension

You can lock a specific row or column in place to make it visible on the screen even when you scroll through the rest of the spreadsheet.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Example of a prompt:

  • “Freeze the top row of the ‘Data converted into Sheet Format’ sheet to make the headers visible.”
  • “Lock the first two columns of the ‘Data converted into Sheet Format’ to keep the ‘YEAR,’ ‘TOURNAMENT,’ and ‘WINNER’ visible while scrolling to the right.” Perform multi-step tasks

To handle complex requests and complete multiple tasks at the same time, combine several actions in a single prompt.

In the side panel, enter your prompt. Examples of prompts:

  • “Clean up this tracker: make the status and priority columns into dropdowns. Add new columns at the end of the table: a new formula column for”Days until due date” (formatted as a number) and a checkbox column for Completed. Finally, highlight due dates in the next two weeks!”
  • “Delete rows where the notes show the seller moved to a new team, highlight in light green sellers achieving more than 120% of quota, then add a new”Notes” column.”
  • “Delete rows where status is archived. Add a new”Team” column between task name and assignee and populate it with a dropdown of Animal themed team names.” Summarize your Drive files with Gemini

You can use Gemini to reference files from your Drive to generate responses in Sheets.

  • On your computer, open a spreadsheet from Google Sheets.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • In the side panel, ask Gemini to use your Drive files to generate text.
    • Example: “What are the main points of: Meeting Notes: Core Team sync.”
  • To check which files were used, below the response, click Expand Sources.
  • (Optional):
    • To add the text to your spreadsheet, click Insert .
    • To view an another version, click Retry .
    • To send feedback about the suggested text, click Good suggestion or Bad suggestion . Summarize your Gmail emails with Gemini

You can use Gemini to reference emails you sent to generate responses.

  • On your computer, open a spreadsheet from Google Sheets.
  • At the top right, click Gemini in Sheets side panel .
  • In the side panel, provide your prompt asking Gemini to reference Gmail email(s).
    • Example: “Catch me up on the latest Monthly Review emails.”
  • To check which files were used, below the response, click Expand Sources.
  • (Optional):
    • To add the text to your spreadsheet, click Insert .
    • To generate a new suggestion, click Retry .
    • To send feedback about the suggested text, click Good suggestion or Bad suggestion . Get help with Google Sheets
  • “Teach me how to use conditional formatting with a color scale.”
  • “How can I remove duplicates?” Get answers from the web

Important: To get answers from the web, make sure to include phrases like “Use Google Search” or “Using web search” in your prompt.

  • “Write a paragraph describing the weather today in Mountain View, California using web search.”
  • “Help me write a paragraph explaining if lightning can strike the same place twice using only information from the web.” Use a Gem

Important: Not all languages support Gems. Learn more about supported languages for Google Workspace with Gemini.

  • On your computer, at the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • On the right, in the side panel, click Gems.
  • Click the Gem you want to use.
  • Select a custom or premade Gem.
    • To start a conversation with the Gem, type a question or prompt at the bottom. Tip: To create a Gem, go to gemini.google.com. You can then use your Gem in the Gemini app and Gemini side panel. Learn how to use Gems in Gemini Apps.

Use Optimization problem solver

You can use the Optimization problem solver to solve operations and logistics tasks, such as allocating budgets, scheduling staff, or optimizing supply chains.

  • On your computer, open a spreadsheet in Google Sheets.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • In the side panel, describe your optimization problem. Example prompts:
    • “I want you to solve a capital budgeting problem. Your main goal is to select the best portfolio of projects to maximize the total Net Present Value.”
    • “I need to minimize total supplier spend. Adjust the order quantities for each supplier to meet my total demand of 1,000 units. Make sure no single supplier provides more than 40% of the total volume.”
    • “I need help with a staffing problem. Determine the minimum number of employees to hire for each of my 7 shift patterns to minimize my total weekly payroll. I must meet my daily staffing requirements, and each employee costs $1,200 per week.”
  • Press Enter.

Collaborate with Gemini on shared or external spreadsheets

You might see a message in the side panel that says, “Warning: Content added by Gemini may be visible to users outside your domain. Use caution with prompts and before enabling search settings.” This message means one of the following:

  • The file has an out-of-domain user with view or edit permissions.
  • The file was created by an out-of-domain user. The file will remain to be classified as “externally accessible” even if the original author(s) removed themselves from the access list.

Get started with Gemini in Sheets

Important: This feature works best with native Google Sheets files. To use Gemini features in an Excel file (.xlsx), click Menu Share & export Save as Google Sheets file.

To use Gemini in Sheets on your mobile device:

  • An eligible Google Workspace or Google AI plan.
  • The Google Sheets app installed on your iPhone or iPad.
  • You need to sign into Google Sheets.
Start a conversation

  • On your iOS device, open the Google Sheets app.

  • At the top right, tap Open Gemini .

  • In the prompt box, enter your question or request.

    • Optional: Tap a suggestion, like Summarize this spreadsheet or Analyze for insights.

  • You can continue the conversation to ask follow up questions or provide more instructions. Note:

  • Data analysis is limited to the active tab in a spreadsheet, and not the full file.

  • Action requests, such as editing or formatting spreadsheets, are currently not supported on iPhone and iPad.

  • Charts generated within the Gemini side panel are limited to static images.

  • Gemini in Sheets on mobile is not available on timeline view tabs.

Customize Gemini in Workspace’s responses with your instructions

Important: Instructions for Gemini in Google Workspace are separate from and do not sync with instructions in Gemini Apps. Learn about instructions for Gemini Apps.

When you add instructions in your personalization settings, you can get tailored, relevant responses in:

  • Chat

  • Docs

  • Drive

  • Gmail

  • Slides For example, when you add instructions, Gemini can adapt its response to your:

  • Role: “When helping me write lesson plans, remember the class is high-school level.”

  • Preferred tone: “Remember to use a professional but enthusiastic tone for my document.”

  • Content: “Always include cost estimations when helping me write a proposal.”

  • Format: “Always summarize my files in bullet points.”

What you need
  • For personal Google Accounts:
    • You must have an eligible Google AI plan:
      • Google AI Plus
      • Google AI Pro
      • Google AI Ultra
    • You can also use personalization settings if your account is enrolled in Google Workspace Experiments, which is a trusted tester program to try new AI features. Learn how to get started with Google Workspace Experiments.
  • For work or school accounts: You need an eligible Google Workspace plan. Learn more about Gemini features and plans.
How instructions work
  • Instructions are on by default in your personalization settings. You can turn them off at any time.
  • Instructions are shared across eligible Workspace products. For example, if you add instructions in Gemini in Gmail, it carries over to Gemini in Docs, Gemini in Slides, and others.
  • You can add up to 1,000 instructions.
  • To check if your instructions are used in a response:
    • Below the response, select Sources.
    • Under “Personalization settings,” find your instructions. Learn how to use sources with Google Workspace with Gemini.
Add instructions for Gemini

Add instructions when you chat with Gemini

When you use instructional phrases, Gemini automatically saves the instruction to your settings. For example, you can say:

  • “From now on, always use short sentences in your responses.”
  • “In the future, remember that I prefer summaries in a list format.” Add instructions in your personalization settings

Important: You can add instructions through personalization settings in Docs, Drive, Gmail, and Slides. In Ask Gemini in Chat, you can only add instructions when you chat with Gemini.

  • On your computer, open a Google Workspace app, like Docs or Gmail.
  • At the top right, select Ask Gemini .
  • At the top left of the Gemini side panel, select Menu Settings Personalization.
  • Select Add.
  • Enter your instructions.
  • Select Save.
Turn your instructions on or off

Important: When off, Gemini provides standard responses. Your saved instructions remain in the list but are not used or deleted.

Turn instructions on or off in Docs, Drive, Gmail & Slides

  • On your computer, open a Google Workspace app, like Docs or Gmail.

  • At the top right, select Ask Gemini .

  • At the top left of the Gemini side panel, select Menu Settings Personalization.

  • At the top, turn Your instructions for Gemini in Workspace on or off . Turn instructions on or off in Ask Gemini in Chat

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .

    • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.

  • In the message box, type /settings.

  • Turn Have Gemini in Workspace use your instructions on or off .

Delete instructions

Important: After you delete an instruction, it’s permanent and can’t be undone.

Delete instructions in Docs, Drive, Gmail & Slides

  • On your computer, open a Google Workspace app, like Docs or Gmail.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • At the top left of the Gemini side panel, select Menu Settings Personalization.
    • To remove specific instructions: Next to the instruction, select Delete .
    • To remove all instructions when you have at least 10 instructions: Select Delete all. Delete instructions in Ask Gemini in Chat
  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
    • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message box, type /settings.
  • At the bottom, select Edit instructions.
  • Next to an instruction, select the checkbox.
  • Select Delete selected instructions.

Customize Gemini in Workspace’s responses with your instructions (Computer)

Important: Instructions for Gemini in Google Workspace are separate from and do not sync with instructions in Gemini Apps. Learn about instructions for Gemini Apps.

When you add instructions in your personalization settings, you can get tailored, relevant responses in:

  • Chat

  • Docs

  • Drive

  • Gmail

  • Slides For example, when you add instructions, Gemini can adapt its response to your:

  • Role: “When helping me write lesson plans, remember the class is high-school level.”

  • Preferred tone: “Remember to use a professional but enthusiastic tone for my document.”

  • Content: “Always include cost estimations when helping me write a proposal.”

  • Format: “Always summarize my files in bullet points.”

What you need
  • For personal Google Accounts:
    • You must have an eligible Google AI plan:
      • Google AI Plus
      • Google AI Pro
      • Google AI Ultra
    • You can also use personalization settings if your account is enrolled in Google Workspace Experiments, which is a trusted tester program to try new AI features. Learn how to get started with Google Workspace Experiments.
  • For work or school accounts: You need an eligible Google Workspace plan. Learn more about Gemini features and plans.
How instructions work
  • Instructions are on by default in your personalization settings. You can turn them off at any time.
  • Instructions are shared across eligible Workspace products. For example, if you add instructions in Gemini in Gmail, it carries over to Gemini in Docs, Gemini in Slides, and others.
  • You can add up to 1,000 instructions.
  • To check if your instructions are used in a response:
    • Below the response, select Sources.
    • Under “Personalization settings,” find your instructions. Learn how to use sources with Google Workspace with Gemini.
Add instructions for Gemini

Add instructions when you chat with Gemini

When you use instructional phrases, Gemini automatically saves the instruction to your settings. For example, you can say:

  • “From now on, always use short sentences in your responses.”
  • “In the future, remember that I prefer summaries in a list format.” Add instructions in your personalization settings

Important: You can add instructions through personalization settings in Docs, Drive, Gmail, and Slides. In Ask Gemini in Chat, you can only add instructions when you chat with Gemini.

  • On your computer, open a Google Workspace app, like Docs or Gmail.
  • At the top right, select Ask Gemini .
  • At the top left of the Gemini side panel, select Menu Settings Personalization.
  • Select Add.
  • Enter your instructions.
  • Select Save.
Turn your instructions on or off

Important: When off, Gemini provides standard responses. Your saved instructions remain in the list but are not used or deleted.

Turn instructions on or off in Docs, Drive, Gmail & Slides

  • On your computer, open a Google Workspace app, like Docs or Gmail.

  • At the top right, select Ask Gemini .

  • At the top left of the Gemini side panel, select Menu Settings Personalization.

  • At the top, turn Your instructions for Gemini in Workspace on or off . Turn instructions on or off in Ask Gemini in Chat

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .

    • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.

  • In the message box, type /settings.

  • Turn Have Gemini in Workspace use your instructions on or off .

Delete instructions

Important: After you delete an instruction, it’s permanent and can’t be undone.

Delete instructions in Docs, Drive, Gmail & Slides

  • On your computer, open a Google Workspace app, like Docs or Gmail.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • At the top left of the Gemini side panel, select Menu Settings Personalization.
    • To remove specific instructions: Next to the instruction, select Delete .
    • To remove all instructions when you have at least 10 instructions: Select Delete all. Delete instructions in Ask Gemini in Chat
  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
    • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message box, type /settings.
  • At the bottom, select Edit instructions.
  • Next to an instruction, select the checkbox.
  • Select Delete selected instructions.

Find & manage your Gemini in Workspace conversation history

Important: This article explains how to manage conversation history for Gemini in Workspace. To manage history in Gemini Apps, use these instructions instead.

You can find and manage your conversation history with Gemini in:

  • Docs
  • Drive
  • Gmail
  • Sheets
  • Slides Your conversation history is app-specific. For example, a conversation with Gemini in Gmail only appears there and not in Gemini in Docs.

How to find, rename, and delete your conversations with Gemini

What you need

To check your conversation history, you need one of the following:

  • A personal Google Account:
    • Google AI Pro
    • Google AI Ultra
    • Google Workspace Experiments
  • A work or school account:
    • You need an eligible Google Workspace plan with access to Gemini Beta. Your administrator controls access to Gemini Beta. If you can’t find this feature, your administrator may not have Beta features enabled for your organization.
Find your conversation history

Important: Your conversation history does not include any interactions with the Gemini side panel that occurred before the release of this feature.

  • On your computer, open a Google Workspace app, like Gmail or Docs.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • At the top left, click More options .
  • Under “History,” select a recent conversation.
    • To find more conversations, click View all conversations. Tip: Your conversations are organized by date, with the most recent at the top.
Resume a past conversation

When you return to a previous conversation, you can continue where you left off.

  • On your computer, open a Google Workspace app, like Gmail or Docs.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • At the top left, click More options .
  • Under “History,” click the conversation you want to open.
    • To find more conversations, click View all conversations.
  • At the bottom, enter a new prompt in the box.
  • Press Enter.
Rename or delete a conversation

To organize your history, you can give your conversations custom names or remove them permanently.

  • On your computer, open a Google Workspace app, like Gmail or Docs.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • At the top left, click More options .
  • Under “History,” hover over a conversation.
    • To find more conversations, click View all conversations.
  • Click More .
  • Select an option:
    • Rename:
      • Enter a new title for the conversation.
      • Press Enter.
    • Delete: To remove the conversation, click Delete.
      • After you delete a conversation, it’s permanent and can’t be undone. Tips: For work or school accounts:
  • If “Delete” is disabled, your organization’s administrator has turned off your ability to delete your history.
  • By default, your conversation history is kept forever. However, your administrator can set an auto-deletion period for your organization.
  • Your administrator can’t recover or access deleted conversations.
Delete your conversation history automatically

Important: For work or school accounts, your administrator controls whether you can change your auto-delete settings. If your auto-delete settings are grayed out, you can’t change them.

You can choose how long Google keeps your Gemini in Workspace history. Only inactive conversations are automatically deleted after the time period you select. For example, if an older conversation is still active, it’s not automatically deleted.

  • On your computer, open a Google Workspace app, like Gmail or Docs.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • At the top left, click More options .
  • Click Settings History.
  • Under “Delete after,” choose an option:
    • 3 months
    • 18 months
    • 36 months
    • Manual deletion only
  • Click Apply.
Learn why some responses aren’t saved

Some responses are temporary and don’t save to your conversation history. For example:

  • System status alerts, such as “You are offline.”
  • Messages not generated by Gemini, such as a confirmation after you export a response to Google Docs.

What you need to use Google Workspace with Gemini
  • Be 18 or over.
  • An eligible Google Account:
    • If you have a work or school Google Account, you can get access to AI-powered features with an eligible Google Workspace plan.
    • If you have a personal Google Account, you can get access to AI-powered features with:
      • Google AI Plus
      • Google AI Pro
      • Google AI Ultra Additional requirements
  • Some AI features may not be available in your language. If you can’t use a feature in your language, you can switch to a supported language in your Google Account. Learn more about supported languages for Google Workspace with Gemini.

Frequently asked questions

How does Google protect my data?

The addition of these AI features includes the same robust data protection and security standards that come with all Google Workspace services:

  • Users get enterprise-grade data protections when they use the Gemini app. Submissions aren’t reviewed by humans or otherwise used to train models.
  • Your interactions with Gemini in Google Workspace apps stay within your organization. Prompts and content you generate with these features is stored alongside your Workspace content and is never shared outside your organization.
  • Your existing Google Workspace protections are automatically applied. These AI features bring the same enterprise-grade security as the rest of Google Workspace, automatically applying your organization’s existing controls and data handling practices, such as data-regions policies and Data Loss Prevention.
  • Your content is not used for any other customers. None of your content is used for model training outside of your domain without permission. Learn how Google Workspace keeps your data secure and prioritizes privacy.

If you have a Google AI plan, learn how Gemini protects your data.

Can I control access to these AI features?

You have the option to turn off some AI features. Learn how to turn Google Workspace smart features on or off.

In addition, if you have a work or school account, your administrator can also:

  • Turn off access to the Gemini App.
  • Turn off Gemini Notebook as an additional service.
  • Stop users from letting Google AI take notes in meetings. Your existing Google Workspace data protections are automatically applied to AI features.

If you have a Google AI plan, learn how Gemini protects your data.

Are there tips for using Gemini effectively?

You can help improve your success with Gemini with these basic best practices:

  • Learn how to write good prompts for Gemini.
  • Use this cheat sheet for an overview of Gemini features.

Learn about AI labels & content credentials

On images, videos, and audio generated by Gemini in supported Workspace apps, you will see “Content Credentials”, a technology that provides media history and transparency about the use of artificial intelligence (AI).

Understand AI labels & content credentials

Important: If the app is listed as “Google Media Processing Services”, it means the file was definitely made or changed using AI. This is the official digital signature for content produced by Google’s generative models.

Hidden digital labels are inside supported files, like images, videos, and audio. They give you details about:

  • Provider: The organization that created or published the content (e.g., Google).

  • App: The specific software or tool used to generate or modify the content. Content credentials can:

  • Provide details about the origin and history of a photo or video through a standard that works across devices and apps from different companies.

  • Provide information from the app or device maker about AI or non-AI tools used to create or edit a photo or video. Content Credentials cannot tell you if a photo or video is real or fake, but you can use the information together with the content of the photo or video to make informed decisions.

Inspect credentials within supported editors

For files opened within the Workspace apps listed below, you might find more specific content credential details. Use the entry point for your editor to view credentials:

  • Docs, Slides, Vids (Web): Right-click/context menu Content credentials sidebar.
  • Sheets (Web): Click the 3-dot menu (floating images) or context menu below “Put image over cells” (embedded images) Content credentials side panel.
  • Google Pics: Main menu Content credentials.
  • Drive Audio Overviews: open File Details to show the Details side panel.
Understand technical limitations

While content credentials offer insights into an asset’s history, they operate within specific technical boundaries.

Platform & encryption limitations
  • Web-only inspection: Content credentials inspection is only available when using Google Workspace on a computer web browser.
  • No client-side encryption (CSE) support: Client-side encrypted files do not support C2PA signing.
  • No offline support: Offline files do not support C2PA signing.
Recognize fragile file history

C2PA metadata can be lost or altered. The “chain of custody” may be broken if:

  • You take a screenshot: A new file is created without the original credentials.
  • You resize or re-save: Using standard image or video editing tools can strip embedded metadata.
  • You use third-party tools: Sharing content via certain social media platforms often removes or modifies original metadata.
  • You download or export the file. Tip: SynthID metadata is preserved during most edits, downloads, and exports.
Learn the difference between content credential history and facts

A valid content credential confirms how a digital file was made or edited. It does not confirm the content’s truth or reality.

For instance, an AI tool might generate a realistic image of an event that never happened. While the content credentials will confirm the image was created by a specific AI tool, they do not verify the truthfulness of the image’s subject matter.

Learn how Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Sheets, Slides, Meet, Vids & Pics protects your data

Across Google and Workspace, we’ve long shared robust privacy commitments that outline how we protect user data and prioritize privacy. Generative AI doesn’t change these commitments — it actually reaffirms their importance.

Our privacy commitments to all Workspace users

Generative AI does not change our foundational privacy protections for giving users choice and control over their data. To that end, here are key facts about how Workspace data is handled.

  • Your data is your data. The content that you put into Google Workspace services (emails, documents, etc.) is yours. We never sell your data, and you can delete your content or export it.
  • Your data stays in Workspace by default. We do not use your Workspace data to train or improve the underlying generative AI and large language models that power Gemini, Search, and other systems outside of Workspace without permission.
  • Your privacy is protected. Interactions with intelligent Workspace features, such as accepting or rejecting spelling suggestions, or reporting spam, are anonymized and/or aggregated and may be used to improve or develop helpful Workspace features like spam protection, spell check, and autocomplete. These Workspace features are developed with strict privacy protections that keep users in control.
  • Your content is not used for ads targeting in Google Workspace. Google Workspace does not collect, scan, or use your content for advertising purposes. Important: If you’re a Workspace user with a personal account and you choose to share data, including your Workspace data, with Gemini Apps or Search services for Personal Intelligence, or through screen actions (including screenshots), this data will be processed according to their respective terms and policies, and may be used for model training and improvement. Learn more in the Gemini Apps Privacy Hub or the Search services Frequently Asked Questions.

These are the privacy commitments that Workspace extends to all of its users. But they aren’t just words. To ensure we continually meet these high standards, independent auditors validate our practices against international standards and best practices.

Specific commitments for Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Slides, Sheets, Meet, Vids & Pics

For users with Google AI plans, when using Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Slides, Sheets, Meet, Vids, and Pics, your data is yours and under your control. Whether you ask Gemini to summarize an email or document, write a blog post, or add a unique image to your slide:

  • Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Slides, Sheets, Meet, Vids, and Pics uses your content in Google Workspace to provide more useful responses to your prompts and doesn’t use your content to train or improve Gemini or other generative AI models.
  • Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Slides, Sheets, Meet, Vids, and Pics doesn’t store your prompt or the generated output without your permission. Note: For users enrolled in the Google Workspace Experiments program, use of Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Slides, Sheets, Meet, Vids, and Pics is covered by the Google Workspace Experiments Privacy Notice & Terms for Personal Accounts.

Learn how to use sources with Google Workspace with Gemini

When you use Gemini in Workspace apps like Docs and Drive, you use sources to tell Gemini exactly which information to use in its response.

Sources are files, documents, or contextual info that Gemini uses to provide more relevant and focused answers to your prompts.

With sources, Gemini can:

  • Find information: Get tailored responses or ask for data points found in your files.
  • Summarize documents: Get a summary or extract key points from a file you have as a source.
  • Compare facts between files: Use multiple source files to compare data, insights, or findings across them.
Understand your sources

When you interact with Gemini, you can manage the content that it can access to inform its response. You can:

  • Add a source from Drive
  • Manage source settings
  • Add a missing source
  • Use cell ranges as a source in Sheets
  • Check sources that contribute to Gemini’s response
Add a source from Drive

You can add specific files in Drive when you want Gemini to prioritize these files before it consults other options. When you add a source, it remains active for your entire conversation, providing consistent context for Gemini’s responses. You can add:

  • Google Docs

  • Google Sheets

  • Google Slides

  • PDFs Add a source in Docs, Gmail, or Slides

  • Go to:

    • Docs: docs.google.com
    • Gmail: mail.google.com
    • Slides: slides.google.com

  • At the top right corner, click Ask Gemini .

  • At the bottom of the panel, click Add sources .

  • Click Add from Drive.

  • Select a file.

  • Click Add. Add a source in Drive

  • Go to drive.google.com.

  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .

  • In the left panel, under “Your sources” or “Project sources,” click Add.

  • Select the files, folders, or emails you want to add as sources.

  • Click Add. Learn how to manage your sources and search settings in Drive.

Add a source in Sheets

  • Go to sheets.google.com.

  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .

  • At the bottom of the panel, click Sheet .

    • If your sheet is not empty, click Sources .

  • Click Add from Drive.

  • Select a file.

  • Click Add. Tips:

  • To add a file, you need permission to access it. You can only use files you have permission to view in Drive as sources. If you lack file access, you get this alert: “You need access to some files.” Learn how to get permission to open a file or folder.

  • Before you can add a PDF as a source, upload it to Drive. Learn how to upload files and folders to Google Drive.

Manage source settings

Important:

  • Gemini only searches the sources you have selected, but may use any app data enabled by an administrator as well as activity from across Workspace apps to prioritize the most relevant information from available sources. Some sources are on by default, and you can disable them in your source settings at any time.

  • Gemini can reference sources from a previous turn in your current conversation. To exclude a source you had previously included, start a new conversation and go to your source settings to select the sources you want. Manage source settings in Docs, Gmail, or Slides

  • Go to:

    • Docs: docs.google.com
    • Gmail: mail.google.com
    • Slides: slides.google.com

  • At the top right corner, click Ask Gemini .

    • In Docs, you can also add sources from the bottom bar.

  • Click Add sources .

  • Click Gemini search settings.

  • Turn specific search locations on or off:

    • Drive search
    • Gmail search
    • Chat search
    • Web search Manage source settings in Drive

Important: When you start a conversation from scratch, search settings for Drive, Gmail, Chat, and Calendar are turned on by default. Gemini uses these default search settings to answer questions. Web search remains off by default. Learn how to manage your sources and search settings in Drive.

  • Go to drive.google.com.
  • At the top right corner, click Ask Gemini .
  • In the left panel, toggle on Let Gemini search for sources. This enables Gemini to pull broader context from across Google Workspace.
  • If you want to limit locations, leave the primary toggle on but uncheck specific locations:
    • Select Drive to search your wider Drive content beyond pinned sources.
    • Select Chat, Calendar, or Gmail to search recent communications and meeting schedules.
    • Select Web to search the internet for supplemental public data. Manage source settings in Sheets
  • Go to sheets.google.com.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • At the bottom of the panel, click Sheet .
    • If your sheet is not empty, click Sources .
  • Click Gemini search settings.
  • Turn specific search locations on or off:
    • Drive search
    • Gmail search
    • Chat search
    • Web search Manage source settings for skills in Workspace Studio

Important: When you build a skill, search settings for Drive and Web are turned on by default. Gemini uses these default search settings to build the skill.

  • Go to Google Workspace Studio.
  • On the left, select Skills.
  • At the top right, click Create.
  • At the bottom of the skill builder, click Add files & more .
  • Select Gemini search settings.
  • Under “Where Gemini can search,” check or uncheck the sources you want Gemini to access:
    • Drive
    • Gmail
    • Chat
    • Calendar
    • Web
Add a missing source

If a prompt requires a source you haven’t selected in your Gemini search settings, you’ll get a message: “To complete this request, Gemini needs access to [service].”

To fix this issue:

  • In the Gemini in Workspace side panel, click Add Gemini search settings.
  • Under “Where Gemini can search,” check the box next to the missing source.
Use cell ranges as a source in Sheets

In Sheets, if you want Gemini to use a specific range or table in the file instead of the entire sheet:

  • Highlight the cell range in your sheet.

  • Ask Gemini a question that references the range. Tips:

  • Cell ranges are only for the sheet tab you are currently on.

  • Gemini in Sheets might automatically select existing sources, such as other Sheet tabs. If you want to ask a question only about your selected cell range, make sure to deselect the other sources first.

Check sources that contribute to Gemini’s response

After Gemini generates a response, you can review a list of the files that contributed to its answer. Below the response from Gemini, select Sources to find the list of sources.

For all requests that you make to Gemini, there’s a limited processing capacity, often referred to as a context window. If you have too many sources, or include sources with too much text, they may exceed this capacity. In these cases, Gemini might base its response on some, but not all, of the content.

Even when Gemini shows sources, it can still get things wrong. For example:

  • Gemini might miss a source it used, or it may cite a document that is not directly used for a specific piece of information.
  • In some cases, Gemini can make up a source, presenting it as factual even if it wasn’t part of the request. Make sure to double-check the response and verify information with the listed sources, and with other sources you trust, before you rely on the generated content.
